h: The Covenant Is Repaired Through Shabbos Torah and Prayer

p: At the second meal of Shabbos we say:
the Holy Ancient One is revealed, etc."
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג רכה, ב)
And in the holy Zohar on this parshah (III 225b):
the rectification of the holy covenant,
and guard it as is fitting, etc."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יב, א)
And this is according to what they said (Chagigah 12a):
"And 'good' is none other than the tzaddik,
'Say of the tzaddik that it is good.'"
that is, the attribute of Malchus;
will be nourished and sustained through you;
you will delight upon Hashem, etc.
through the rectification of the covenant;
דְּבָרָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּגְנִיז לֵיהּ
that the Holy One, blessed is He, created and hid away,
and to which Aharon the Kohen was bound, etc."
that was hidden away for the tzaddikim;
and a tzaddik is called one who guards the covenant;
for it is impossible to merit this light
except through the attribute of the tzaddik.
And it says, "once the covenant is rectified,
for this is the root and beginning of the blemish
and on account of this came all the exiles;
and the root of the exile of Egypt
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, יב)
and fenced himself off from immorality,
and all the males were fenced off in his merit."
that the sale of Yosef as a slave
was because he said about them
that they raised their eyes, etc.;
and they knew that they were clean,
and thought that "whoever disqualifies, disqualifies with his own blemish,"
and he needed refining in this,
and there in Egypt they were all refined.
are mainly to rectify this blemish,
and through the rectification of this blemish
they merit afterward the primordial light.
which corresponds to the attribute of Atika Kadisha,
it is written, "Then you shall delight upon Hashem,"
which is the aspect of Atika,
as is written in the holy Zohar
(Yisro, there, and end of parshas Acharei),
that is, the thorn of the yud
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג סה, ב)
(as is written in the holy Zohar III 65b);
and Atika Kadisha is called Ayin,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב סד, ב)
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא, חֵלֶק ג יא, ב)
And in the holy Zohar (Vayikra, III 11b)
it counts "Let there be light" as the first saying;
that is, after the primordial light was hidden away
and is concealed from all thought,
then it is counted as the first saying
through rectifying the attribute of the tzaddik.
And the main rectification for this
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
is only through words of Torah,
for in holiness it is called "holy flesh,"
and on the opposite side it is called "the flesh of donkeys";
was hidden away in words of Torah;
in the saying "Let there be light"
correspond to the five books of the Torah
and Shabbos is in the secret of the covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, א)
for on Shabbos is the time for words of Torah,
all six days of the week:
it establishes the one who said in the Yerushalmi
only to toil in words of Torah,"
and therefore then is the time
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קיח, ב)
That is why it is stated in the Gemara (Shabbos 118b)
and in the Midrashim and the holy Zohar
that through keeping Shabbos according to its law
And Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
was the first to merit words of Torah;
"'Let there be light': this is Avraham";
that is, the saying "Let there be light"
was said on the first day,
which is the attribute of Chessed.
That is why at the second meal, of Atika,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
it is written, "Then you shall delight upon Hashem,"
"And it shines with the primordial light, etc.,"
and Avraham is a chariot for the attribute of Chessed,
and so it is written of him (Tehillim 110:4):
and likewise Aharon the Kohen, his attribute is Chessed.
And this is why the holy Zohar says:
and to which Aharon the Kohen was bound";
and called Aharon by the name "the Kohen,"
on which the saying "Let there be light" was said.
That is why at this meal we say,
that He hid away for the tzaddikim.

p: And the pasuk opened, "Trust in Hashem,"
for the main thing is through trust in Hashem,
to be able to rectify the blemish;
"The face of Hashem is against evildoers,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ריט, ב)
and so it is in the Gemara (Niddah 13b).
"They cried out, and Hashem heard, etc.,"
for crying out helps for this;
and He saves those crushed in spirit":
the main thing is that he cry out
with a broken and crushed heart.
And likewise David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
in the psalm he composed about teshuvah,
for he came to teach teshuvah to the individual
and therefore they ascribed this blemish to him:
"The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit;
O God, You will not despise."
"Woe to the wicked, it is evil";
one who hates the attribute of the tzaddik,
"Hashem redeems the soul of His servants" (ibid. 23):
these are the ones who need rectification and redemption;
"and none who take refuge in Him shall be held guilty":
by implication it speaks of one who blemished,
for one would have thought they would be held guilty;
why does it say "they shall not be held guilty"?
And since they take refuge in Hashem Yisbarach,
they shall not be held guilty.
And this is what the holy Zohar mentioned says:
That is, the main rectification for this
and crying out with a broken heart
and Shabbos is the time of Torah, as stated.
And Tanna D'vei Eliyahu expounds the pasuk
"Where is the place of My rest"
"But to this one will I look,
to the poor and contrite of spirit,
for on Shabbos the Jew becomes
and then is the time to rectify this blemish.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּמִּזְמוֹר שֶׁל שַׁבָּת (תְּהִלִּים צב, ב)
And this is what is said in the psalm of Shabbos (Tehillim 92:2):
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem":
"good" is the attribute of the tzaddik,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב
as it says, "Say of the tzaddik that it is good";
"But whoever confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy"
(as is written in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer);
for then is the time to rectify the attribute of the tzaddik,
And this is why it counts (Zohar Chadash, Toldos)
the Mussaf of Shabbos opposite Yosef HaTzaddik;
that is, the added holiness from Shabbos
corresponds to the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik;
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא)
that it be "and your people are all righteous" (Yeshayahu 60:21);
for "whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב כג, א)
as is written in the holy Zohar (II 23a);
and this will become clear in the Time to Come.
And Shabbos is a semblance of Olam Haba,
and then a semblance of this becomes clear.
And this is what is stated in the holy Zohar,
that Shabbos is in the secret of the covenant,
for in it is the time to rectify "and do good."
which is the attribute of Malchus,
for the meal of Shabbos is "the meal of faith,"
as is written in the holy Zohar (Yisro 88);
that he be sustained through the faith above;
and then "you shall delight upon Hashem"
and this is what they said, "His light dwells upon it."
And the haftarah passage opens with keeping Shabbos
"Fortunate is the man who does this, etc.,
and let not the foreigner say,
who has joined himself to Hashem, saying:
Hashem will surely separate me from His people;
and let not the eunuch say:
Behold, I am a dry tree, etc."
And what is its connection here?
But according to what was said,
that Shabbos is a semblance of Olam Haba,
and "and your people are all righteous" becomes clear,
have a portion in Olam Haba;
is one who spoiled in this matter:
"Hashem will surely separate me from His people";
and let not the eunuch say,
for there it speaks of eunuchs
whom the king of Babylon castrated
and since this happened to them,
that they were castrated by the king of Babylon;
they would also say that they are denied
which is "at the same time of life, etc."
וְכֵן לִפְעָמִים יֵשׁ תִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי בָּנִים
and sometimes there is rectification through children,
"a son brings merit to his father"
"For thus says Hashem to the eunuchs
which is to be laborers of Torah,
שֶׁכָּל עִסְקוֹ יִהְיֶה רַק דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
that all his occupation be only words of Torah,
for this is the will of the Omnipresent,
as has been explained several times
"when they do the will of the Omnipresent"
and "when they do not do His will,"
meaning that they fulfill only the mitzvah
(and it was explained in parshas Lech, maamar 3);
to hold fast to the holiness of Shabbos,
which is in the secret of the covenant,
the days of work as well.
"And I will give them in My house and within My walls
"For My house shall be a house of prayer";
That is, through Torah and prayer
one attains a broken and crushed heart;
and both of them we merit on Shabbos,
who is called "a man of delights";
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאֵצֶל יוֹסֵף נֶאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, ו)
that is, regarding Yosef it is said (Bereishis 39:6):
"handsome of form and handsome of appearance,"
for his attribute is called so;
and likewise all "the beautiful ones of Yerushalayim,"
and wherever they praised someone's beauty,
it does not mean beauty of the body,
רַק שֶׁהָיָה הַגּוּף נָאֶה וְנָקִי מִפְּגָם זֶה
but that the body was fine and clean of this blemish;
"I come from the seed of Yosef"
And so I heard from our holy Rebbe,
"Are you not like the children of the Kushim"
who is not clean of this blemish
(and this was explained at length elsewhere).
And Daniel is called "a man of delights,"
for he was pleasant to look at;
that is, he was clean of this blemish;
and he was among the eunuchs,
as they said in the Gemara mentioned.
the blemish of the world in this,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה נג, ד-ה)
along the lines of what is written (Yeshayahu 53:4-5):
and he was wounded because of our transgressions";
"The anointed of Hashem was caught in their pits."
"The Holy One, blessed is He, wished
"And of your sons whom you will father they will take,
and they will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."
it is written in the Gemara that he will be killed;
אַךְ הָרַבִּי מִלּוּבְּלִין זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
but the Rebbe of Lublin, of blessed memory,
said that this decree has already been annulled.
לֹא יִהְיֶה גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן עַל יָדוֹ
the complete rectification will not be through him;
that is, the attribute of Yosef
is a tzaddik who never spoiled,
and the majority of the community
who "raised up the yoke of teshuvah"
and Mashiach will be "an individual who did teshuvah,
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven"
that is, he will bring thoughts of teshuvah
And Chizkiyahu, whom He wished to make Mashiach,
that the rectification of this blemish was still lacking,
and it still needed to be rectified
who would come from his sons,
for the time had not yet come.
And Shabbos is the secret of the covenant,
and the time to rectify the blemish
וְאָז יִהְיוּ מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין מִכֹּל וָכֹל
and then they will immediately be redeemed entirely.
